---
title: "Analysis"
---

This example uses built-in R data to model how fuel efficiency changes with weight and horsepower.

## Summarise the data

```{r}
summary(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])
```

## Visualise the relationship

```{r}
plot(
  mtcars$wt,
  mtcars$mpg,
  pch = 19,
  col = "steelblue",
  xlab = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
  ylab = "Miles per gallon",
  main = "Weight compared with fuel efficiency"
)
abline(lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars), col = "firebrick", lwd = 2)
```

## Fit a simple model

```{r}
fuel_model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
coef(summary(fuel_model))
```

## Interpreting the output

In this example, heavier cars tend to have lower fuel efficiency. Adding horsepower to the model helps explain extra variation, which gives a stronger evidence-based conclusion than relying on a graph alone.
